mutant.description: A REAL PLANTED MUTANT, and it is the centre of this cell rather than a formality. One U+2014 em dash was planted into a CLEAN, ASCII, valid-JSON file, and the two real writers were then run over it in their exact source forms -- record-terraform-deploy.sh's bare `open()` read at :259 with its `json.dump` write at :340, and build-and-upload.sh's node `JSON.stringify` updater. The question the mutant answers is not 'does the fix work' but 'where does the corruption come from'.
mutant.expected: If the recorder is merely FRAGILE to inherited mojibake, as row Z-S12 originally claimed, the planted character should survive the round trip unchanged and nothing should break. If instead the pipeline MANUFACTURES the corruption, the character should multiply and the file should eventually become unreadable to the very tool that wrote it.
mutant.observed: IT MANUFACTURES IT. pass 0, one U+2014. pass 1 (recorder read + write), the single character has BECOME THREE, U+00E2 U+20AC U+201D, and the file still looks ASCII because json.dump escapes them, so nothing complains. pass 2 (node re-write), those three are re-emitted as literal UTF-8 bytes. pass 3 (recorder read), UnicodeDecodeError on byte 0x9d. That reproduces the MX-s-3 failure state INCLUDING THE EXACT BYTE VALUE, from a clean file, in three passes. It also explains a symptom the 'fragile reader' story does not: why the file broke in September after months of silence -- it had been corrupting quietly all along and finally produced a byte cp1252 has no character for. Filed as row NFRA_MCPINDEX-Z-S13, which narrows and corrects my own Z-S12 (including its INERT hazard call, now ARMED).

determinism.method: Three re-reads of state that must not move: the acceptance check re-run after the recorder had written the file again; the recorder's own computed last_deployed_commit compared against the value hand-written under MX-s-3; and a bare default-codepage `open()` of the file, which is the exact call that used to raise.
determinism.observed: The file still reads 0 non-ASCII characters AFTER the recorder ran over it -- the property is stable under its own worst writer, because cp1252-reading pure ASCII is lossless and the loop has nothing left to mangle. The recorder independently computed 753fe90fb1, the same value hand-written under MX-s-3, so two routes agree. `json.load(open(path))` with no encoding argument returns 218 functions where it previously raised UnicodeDecodeError at 32218. A SECOND MEASUREMENT OF MINE WAS INVALID AND ITS CONTROL CAUGHT IT: my first node arm read 0 non-ASCII and I nearly recorded 'the writers agree'; node had exited rc=1 and the bytes I read were python's. A second attempt also failed (rc=1, wrong argv index). Only the third run -- rc=0 AND a positive control proving node had actually rewritten the file -- gave the real answer, which was the OPPOSITE of the first reading.
